id: AT-AP-13 (own rows, fork and bg copies)
note: Forks re-ask: the quote check counts only rows this session wrote after it started (its first per-process record, stamped in milliseconds; an older stamp without a fraction is rounded up to the next second). Claude Code 2.1.309 writes the rows a --fork-session resume or a background copy (sessionKind bg) carries over with the new session's id, the parent's uuids and times and no marker, so they are told apart by time; a /branch copy also has forkedFrom. Not counted: a copied typed row, a yes after a copied question, a copied dialog (ask and answer), a bg copy's carried row, a row 5 ms before the record, a row from a fraction-less record's own second, an own yes that answers a copied question, an own answer to a copied dialog, an own row without a timestamp, a forkedFrom row; a session with no record is not checked (unchecked, never a miss). Counted: a launch prompt 50 ms after the record, the bg session's own typed words, an own yes after an own question, an own dialog. Carry: a clear or handoff-resume predecessor's checked approval carries; a fork, bg-copy, none, missing or unknown link carries none; fork and bg-copy predecessors stay own for commands (locate relation successor). Review round 2: a line moved for a quote found only in copied rows (a copied typed row or dialog, a bg copy's row, a row before the record, a forkedFrom row) names the copy as its reason; an own yes to a copied question keeps the short-quote rule, and a row without a timestamp keeps the plain rule. 0.1.4: an own answer to a copied dialog names the copy too (A-8, U-8); a short quote in a copied row after another copied typed row no longer has the copied question before it as its context, so it keeps the short-quote rule (A-5, U-15); a quote first seen in a copied row and later in an own pasted message keeps the first reason, the copy (A-5, U-16).
